entries.title: Job 1:1
segments:
Uz; a district in Arabia, east of Palestine. 
 
  Perfect and upright; a man who habitually feared God and obeyed all his commandments.  Like Zachariah and Elizabeth, he was "righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless."

Feared God; with childlike, reverential, holy fear. 
 
  Eschewed; departed from, avoided. 
 
God sometimes bestows on his children great wealth, numerous friends, and abundance of earthly blessings, and thus increases their obligations to love and serve him.

entries.title: Job 1:4
segments:
. 
 
It is proper to partake of the bounties of Providence with gratitude and joy; and pleasant when brothers and sisters love one another, rejoice in each other's society, and together celebrate the goodness of God.

entries.title: Job 1:5
segments:
Sent and sanctified them; he directed them to perform those outward cleansings which were a sign of that purity of heart and life which God requires of all his worshippers, and Job inculcated on his children by both precept and example. 
 
  Cursed God in their hearts; dishonored him by unworthy and wicked thoughts of him. 
 
  Thus did Job continually; habitually, after each yearly feast of his assembled households. 
 
Seasons of feasting are seasons of peculiar danger.  While men partake freely of God's gifts they are tempted to forget or in some other way to dishonor the giver, and thus they need his pardoning mercy through Jesus Christ.

entries.title: Job 1:9
segments:
For naught; without being paid for it.  Satan means to insinuate that Job's piety is wholly selfish, and will vanish as soon as he finds that it ceases to bring to him a reward of earthly good. 
 
Those who contend that all religion is selfish, and that good men serve God only because he does them good, resemble Satan and take part with him in promoting his cause.

entries.title: Job 1:10
segments:
Made a hedge about him; to defend him from all evil. 
 
  Blessed the work of his hands; rewarded him abundantly for his seeming piety.

entries.title: Job 1:11
segments:
Touch all that he hath; destroy it. 
 
  Curse thee to thy face; openly, with daring impiety.

entries.title: Job 1:12
segments:
Upon himself put not forth thy hand; do not injure him in his person. 
 
Satan, if permitted by God, may not only tempt men to sin, but bring upon them great and sore calamities.

entries.title: Job 1:17
segments: The Chaldeans; a troop of pillagers from near the Euphrates.

entries.title: Job 1:20
segments:
Rent his mantle, and shaved his head; in token of deep mourning. 
 
Good men will not overlook God's hand when calamities come upon them, nor fail to humble themselves before him.

entries.title: Job 1:21
segments:
Shall I return thither; to the womb of the earth, which is the mother of all mankind.  He uses the word "womb" in a twofold sense, first literally, and then figuratively. 
 
Nothing so sustains the soul in the day of severe trial, as the thought that God sends it.

entries.title: Job 1:22
segments: Charged God foolishly; that is, attributed folly to God.
